attempts.validity: blockers COMPLETE, other edges 2, pool timeouts 100

report.summary: Transfer failures and slowness coincide with a config change at 15:11:41 that shrank the DB pool (10→2, timeout 30000→250 ms), plus an idle-in-transaction session blocking writers. Outbox delivery is healthy.

findings.claim: Pool was cut to max 2 connections with a 250 ms acquire timeout at the 15:11:41 restart, and acquisition timeouts followed.
findings.reason: Config changed at 15:11:41; pool shows 100 acquisition timeouts and acquire max 261 ms vs 250 ms timeout.

findings.claim: An idle-in-transaction non-app session held locks, blocking two ledger_app sessions for up to 1.7 s from 15:11:42 to 15:12:58.
findings.reason: Sessions 46083 and 46084 waited on 46085 (idle in transaction) in 22 samples each.

findings.claim: Transfers show 18.8% server errors (42×500, 59×503) and p95 1.6 s. This is likely pool exhaustion amplified by the blocked sessions holding the 2 connections.
findings.reason: Errors and latency align with the small pool and lock waits. Per-request error causes were not observed directly.

findings.claim: Outbox delivery is not the cause: all 431 deliveries succeeded in about 71 ms, with none failed and arrivals equal to publications.
findings.reason: Zero failures, no arrivals minus publications gap, and the consumer is fast.

limitations: Blocker sampling is every 2 s and pool gauges every 5 s, so brief saturation may be missed. Counters restarted, so counts span restarts.
No per-request error messages were seen, so the 500/503 attribution to pool timeouts is inferred.
next_checks: Identify session 46085 (the idle-in-transaction holder) and why its transaction was left open.
Revert pool settings to max 10 / 30000 ms timeout, or justify the change, and re-measure the transfer error ratio.

alternatives.reason: Delivery p95 was 79.5 ms with all attempts successful.
alternatives.hypothesis: Slow downstream consumer causing transfer latency

alternatives.reason: The two effects overlap in time and cannot be separated from these data.
alternatives.hypothesis: The blocking idle-in-transaction session alone explains the errors, independent of pool size

report.summary: A restart at 15:11:41 cut the DB pool from 10 to 2 connections with a 250 ms timeout. An idle-in-transaction session then held locks, so requests timed out acquiring connections and returned 500/503.

findings.claim: Config changed at 15:11:41 restart: poolMaximumSize 10→2 and connection timeout 30000→250 ms.
findings.reason: Runtime config shows the new values from 15:11:41, inside the window.

findings.claim: The undersized pool exhausted: 100 acquisition timeouts, with pending borrowers and active connections above zero from 15:11:08 to 15:12:58.
findings.reason: Pool metrics show timeouts at max 2 and a 250 ms timeout, in the window after the restart.

findings.claim: An idle-in-transaction session blocked two ledger_app sessions for up to 1.7 s (15:11:42-15:12:58). Held connections plus the tiny pool and short timeout likely produced the errors.
findings.reason: The blocking period matches the pool pressure. Transfers show 42×500 and 59×503 (18.8% errors) and p95 1.6 s.

findings.claim: The outbox and consumer are healthy and are not the cause: arrivals equal publications, there are no failures, and delivery takes about 71 ms.
findings.reason: All 431 deliveries succeeded with zero failed. The dips in arrivals and publications coincide with the pool-starved period.

limitations: Blocker sampling is every 2 s, and the identity and origin of the idle-in-transaction session (role 'other') are unknown.
Counters restarted twice, so the error counts mix pre-restart and post-restart traffic. 16 gauge samples were NaN.
next_checks: Identify session 46085 (its application and query) and why it stayed idle in transaction.
Check who changed the pool settings, and whether 5xx errors stop after restoring poolMaximumSize and the timeout.

alternatives.reason: Blocking was short (max 1.7 s). Acquisition timeouts at the 250 ms limit with max 2 connections explain the 5xx errors, and the 10-connection pool would likely have absorbed the blocking.
alternatives.hypothesis: The idle-in-transaction blocker alone caused the failures, independent of the pool change.

alternatives.reason: Consumer deliveries all succeeded in about 71 ms.
alternatives.hypothesis: Downstream consumer slowness caused the failures.
